analysis: Only the BASE text of ClusterOnboardingLive.swift (lines 894-1622) and a truncated patch excerpt were supplied; no HEAD text was visible. Changed ranges: scope is threaded through planModels (new ClusterControlRequest(op: .planModels, scope: context.settings.servingScope)), through the forwarded .planModels/.adopt handlers (request.scope passed to localPlanModels/localAdopt), and a new planningScope(_:) helper (HEAD ~606-616) defaults to .publicServing. In the base units I examined, the changed areas are localAdopt (base 1044-1073) and the replan call at 1073. These are cluster-onboarding control flow over the paired Thunderbolt link (pairing, claim, localToken). The excerpt shows no weakening of pairing/claim checks, artifact digest verification (ClusterCatalogArtifact.sameEntry/filesDigest, manifest-verified downloads), or the stop/drain custody ordering. The scope value is supplied by a paired peer in a forwarded request; the local-only versus public decision affects whether a coordinator is contacted. Whether a forwarded request.scope is authenticated and validated by the receiving Mac (the pairing/claim path in command()), and whether a peer could force a different serving scope than the user chose, cannot be verified from the supplied excerpt. No finding is raised because the HEAD implementation is not visible. Residual questions for integration: how localPlanModels(scope:) and localAdopt(scope:) consume the scope (discoveryMode selection, ClusterPlacementTensorAssistantSelection), and whether a forwarded scope can silently switch a local-only cluster to coordinator-registered serving (relevant to the TB-011/TB-002 coordinator contracts). The relevant threat T-041 (cache) is unrelated to this change. Coverage is limited to base text plus a partial patch.
